operation.note: Camera-only probe snapshot plus offline decode. No Host, no claim, no Ditoo.

method: Six/eight webcam stills captured with the probe snapshot mode, pushed through the real host/frame_transform.py production transform, then decoded with host/motion_truth.py.

findings.framing: PASS. The stimulus fills the webcam ROI and every accepted frame decoded with correct sync corners.
findings.rolling_shutter_tearing: Confirmed on BOTH the operator phone and the webcam. A pre-Gray webcam still read 60 counts backwards (3579 -> 3519 -> 3579); the operator phone still decoded 1255 against a screen readout of 1252. After Gray coding, two independent thresholding methods disagreed on one frame by exactly 1 count, which is the designed bound.
findings.illumination_gradient: Sync corner (3,0) read 98 luma in one frame versus 152-226 elsewhere, while blacks stayed tight at 13-16. That frame was REJECTED, not misdecoded.
findings.threshold_decision: Fixed 128 threshold retained. An adaptive k-means threshold was evaluated and agreed with it on every frame except one torn frame where the two differed by exactly 1 count, so adaptivity buys nothing and adds a misdecode path. The four sync cells sit at the panel corners, which are the most vignetted positions, so they fail before interior data cells dim: rejection is the failure mode, not silent bit flips.
findings.rejection_rate: 1 of 7 frames. Safe and well within budget: 240 fps footage of a 10 s trial yields ~2400 frames against a 30-transition bar.

not_evidence_of: Framing and decode only. No transport, no latency, and no physical panel behaviour is established here.
